chunks: And Sāliḥ al-Ṣayrāfī narrated from ‘Imrān al-Mīthamī, from Sāliḥ ibn Mītham, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever desires to be at the tables of light on the Day of Judgment, let him be among the visitors of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him).

key_terms.زُوَّارِ: Visitors (specifically in the context of Ziyārah)
key_terms.مَوَائِدِ النُّورِ: Tables of light (symbolizing honor and sustenance in the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Husain according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to establish Ziyarat al-Husayn as a means of attaining divine honor, specifically the 'tables of light' (Mawā'id al-Nūr), which symbolize the highest status in Paradise. This narration underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the intercessory and spiritual efficacy of visiting the Ahl al-Bayt, linking earthly devotion directly to eschatological reward.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Sāliḥ Al-Sayrafi narrated from ‘Imrān Al-Maythami, from Sāliḥ ibn Maytham, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
Those who desire sitting at MAWĀ`ID made of light on the Day of Judgment should go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.).
